summary: A proposal for a standard list of six-character host names for Telnet programs, so users would not need to learn each site's own abbreviations. It lists names for the hosts then on the network and asks for objections before a policy date. It was replaced by RFC 247.

eli5.summary: Everybody used different nicknames for the same computers. This note suggests one agreed list of short names so people stop getting confused.

subtitle: A 1971 proposal to give every Telnet program the same short names for network hosts.

tldr.problem: Each Telnet implementation had its own list of host mnemonics, so users had to learn every site's idiosyncrasies, especially when chained through several hosts.
tldr.mechanism: The note proposes one standard list of six-character host designators, paired with host numbers, and asks for objections by 3 October.
tldr.outcome: This proposal was obsoleted by RFC 247, which carries the idea forward.

today: RFC 226 was obsoleted by RFC 247, so it is a historical proposal rather than a current list.

sections.title: The Problem With Host Mnemonics
sections.content:
In each Telnet implementation, a list of host mnemonics lets the user say which serving host they want. At the time, each site used its own special list.

That forced users to be aware of the idiosyncrasies of every list, especially when chained through several hosts via Telnet. It was therefore recommended that standard host designators be adopted.
sections.eli5: Every school used a different nickname for the same computer. That is confusing, so the note asks everyone to use the same nicknames.

sections.title: The Proposed List
sections.content:
The RFC proposes a list of six character designators. Each entry pairs a host number with a designator: for example host 1 is UCLA, host 2 is SRIARC, host 3 is UCSB, host 4 is UTAH and host 145 is MITRE.

Several sites with more than one host get a name for each, such as host 65 as UCLA36 and host 133 as BBNB. Host 158 is listed as TIP.
sections.eli5: It is like a class list that gives every computer one short name next to its number, so everybody calls it the same thing.

sections.title: Schedule and Outcome
sections.content:
Objections were to be registered by 3 October with P. Karp at MITRE. An official policy and implementation date would be set on 8 October.

The unit metadata records that RFC 247 later obsoleted this note.
sections.eli5: People had a couple of weeks to say if they disliked the plan. After that, the rule would be made official.
